decisions.reason: As a core process-equipment product in a niche industrial portfolio, it likely remains worth keeping because uncertainty about long-run demand can still resolve through distributor channels and the carrying cost is moderate.
A second resin injection unit plausibly serves a different specification set, so management would usually keep this option open while market feedback accumulates unless support costs rise sharply.
An automatic airless spray gun fits closely with the firm's established application-technology business, making it a relatively low-cost option to retain on the market.

The manual airless spray gun is highly complementary to the firm's existing spray equipment range, so a medium German machinery firm would tend to continue offering it unless clear commercial failure appears.
Because the air-assisted airless spray gun extends the core gun portfolio into another application niche, keeping it preserves upside while requiring limited additional commitment.
The data logger appears to have lost prominence quickly and is more peripheral to the firm's mechanical core, so real-options logic favors abandoning it once early signals are weak.
